question.problem:
Consider the differential equation ${y}^{″}+4{\pi }^{2}y=f(x),$ where the $2$-periodic forcing function is given by 

$$
f(x)∼3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below regarding the resonant component of a particular solution of the equation.

The natural frequency of the system matches the frequency of the {{field-1}} harmonic of the forcing function. 

Consequently, the particular solution contains a resonant term of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{2}}={{field-2}}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We begin by identifying resonance. The differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+4{\pi }^{2}y=f(x)
$$

has a natural frequency of 

$$
\omega =\sqrt{4{\pi }^{2}}=2\pi .
$$

The frequencies of the forcing harmonics for a $2$-periodic function $(L=1)$ are 

$$
{\omega }_{n}=\frac{n\pi }{1}=n\pi .
$$

For $n=2$, we have ${\omega }_{2}=2\pi .$ Since ${\omega }_{2}=\omega ,$ the $n=2$ harmonic of the forcing function causes resonance.

For the $n=2$ harmonic, the forcing term is 

$$
{f}_{2}(x)=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x).
$$

Because this frequency matches the natural frequency, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{2}}=x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{{p}_{2}}^{′} & =(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x))+x(-2\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)+2\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)) \\ {y}_{{p}_{2}}^{″} & =-4\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)+4\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)-4{\pi }^{2}x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x))\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{{p}_{2}}^{″}$ and ${y}_{{p}_{2}}$ into the equation ${y}^{″}+4{\pi }^{2}y=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x):$

$$
[-4\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)+4\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)-4{\pi }^{2}{y}_{{p}_{2}}]+4{\pi }^{2}{y}_{{p}_{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)
$$

The resonant terms involving $x$ cancel out, leaving

$$
-4\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)+4\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x).
$$

Now, equating the sine and cosine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-4\pi A=0 \\ 4\pi B=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}A=0 \\ B=\frac{1}{16\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resonant component of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{{p}_{2}}=\frac{x}{16\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x).
$$
